import pandas as pd
import io
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """survived,pclass,sex,age,sibsp,parch,fare,embarked,class,who,adult_male,deck,embark_town,alive,alone
0,3,male,22.0,1,0,7.25,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,False
1,1,female,38.0,1,0,71.2833,C,First,woman,False,C,Cherbourg,yes,False
1,3,female,26.0,0,0,7.925,S,Third,woman,False,,Southampton,yes,True
1,1,female,35.0,1,0,53.1,S,First,woman,False,C,Southampton,yes,False
0,3,male,35.0,0,0,8.05,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,True
"""

# Load the dataset into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes for two subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 6))
fig.suptitle('Titanic Survival Analysis: Key Factors', fontsize=16)

# Plot 1: Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex
# We use a barplot to show the mean survival rate (y='survived') for each category.
# 'errorbar=None' removes confidence intervals, making the plot cleaner for small datasets.
sns.barplot(x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', data=df, ax=axes[0], palette='viridis', errorbar=None)
axes[0].set_title('Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Passenger Class')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Survival Rate')
# Customize x-axis labels for clarity
axes[0].set_xticks([0, 1, 2])
axes[0].set_xticklabels(['1st Class', '2nd Class', '3rd Class'])
axes[0].legend(title='Sex')

# Plot 2: Age Distribution by Survival Status
# Given the very small dataset size, a boxplot is more appropriate than a KDE plot
# to visualize the distribution of age across survival status without over-interpreting sparse data.
# Drop rows with missing age values for this plot, though in this sample, all ages are present.
df_age_cleaned = df.dropna(subset=['age'])
sns.boxplot(x='survived', y='age', data=df_age_cleaned, ax=axes[1], palette='coolwarm')
axes[1].set_title('Age Distribution by Survival Status')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Survival Status')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Age')
# Customize x-axis labels for clarity
axes[1].set_xticks([0, 1])
axes[1].set_xticklabels(['Died', 'Survived'])

# Adjust layout to prevent titles/labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png')
